findings.title: Unsubscribe writes notification_level directly, so auto-tracking can silently undo it
findings.body: `tu.save!` changes notification_level without going through `TopicUser.change`. `TopicUser.change` also sets `notifications_reason_id` (user_changed) and `notifications_changed_at`, and publishes the change on MessageBus. Here the reason stays NULL for any topic whose level the user never explicitly set. `TopicUser.update_last_read` (the CASE expression in topic_user.rb) and `TopicUser.auto_track` both switch a topic to tracking when `notifications_reason_id IS NULL` and the user's viewing time passes the auto-track threshold. So after a user clicks the unsubscribe link and the topic is muted, the next read can flip it back to tracking, and the promise in the email to stop notifications is silently broken. Use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, topic.id, notification_level: ...)` instead.

findings.title: State-changing unsubscribe is exposed on GET with no CSRF protection
findings.body: The action mutates notification_level, but it is reachable via GET (config/routes.rb: `get 't/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe'` and `get 't/:topic_id/unsubscribe'`). Rails' forgery protection does not cover GET, so any page that embeds the URL (for example an img tag on another site) will mute a logged-in user's topic. Mail link scanners and prefetchers will also trigger the mutation without the user clicking. A state change like this should be a POST (with a GET confirmation page), or should use a signed token like the existing email/unsubscribe/:key flow.

findings.title: Nil TopicUser dereference when no membership row exists
findings.body: `TopicUser.find_by` can return nil (for example if the row was never created or was removed), and `tu.notification_level` is then called without a guard, which raises NoMethodError and returns a 500. Using `TopicUser.change`, which creates the row when it is missing, would avoid this and also fix the persistence problem noted for the save! call.

findings.title: Unsubscribe only steps watching/tracking down to regular, contradicting the email text
findings.body: The email copy says 'You will stop receiving notifications for <title>', but for users at tracking or watching the action sets notification_level to regular. Regular still sends notifications for replies and mentions, so those users keep getting notified. Only users already at regular are muted. Either mute for every level or change the wording.

findings.title: track_visit! uses the topic id as the user id when given an integer user id
findings.body: `user_id = user.is_a?(User) ? user.id : topic` falls back to `topic`, which is the topic id, instead of `user`. TopicsController calls `TopicUser.track_visit! topic_id, user_id` with integer ids, so `user_id` becomes the topic id. The update then hits (or creates) the topic_users row for whichever user has the same id as the topic, and the real user's last_visited_at is never recorded. This predates the PR, but the PR edits this same method (line 125), so the fix belongs in this change.

findings.title: add_unsubscribe_link now requires unsubscribe_url or email building raises
findings.body: The unsubscribe_link string now interpolates %{unsubscribe_url}. html_part (line 67) and body (line 90) call I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args), and template_args only contains unsubscribe_url if the caller passed it. Any caller that sets add_unsubscribe_link: true without unsubscribe_url, including plugins that use this public builder, will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument while building the email. Either default the URL in the builder or render the topic line only when the URL is present.

findings.title: Unrelated summary route constraint silently removed
findings.body: The diff rewrites the summary routes and drops `post_number: /<digits>/` from their constraints (both `t/:slug/:topic_id/summary` and `t/:topic_id/summary`). The unsubscribe feature has nothing to do with summary URLs, and the change is not mentioned. Either revert it or explain why it is safe, since the constraint's effect on a route with no post_number segment is not obvious.

findings.title: Route name and template path do not match, so the unsubscribe template may never render
findings.body: The route is declared as a top-level `this.route('topicUnsubscribe', ...)`. Ember derives the default template name from the route name (topicUnsubscribe, or topic-unsubscribe), not from the path topic/unsubscribe, so the new templates/topic/unsubscribe.hbs is likely not the template used for this route. The page could render blank or fall back to the application template. Either rename the template to match the route or nest the route under the topic resource as this.route('unsubscribe'). I have not verified the resolver behavior in the running app.

findings.title: New unsubscribe action has no specs
findings.body: Nothing covers the new action: the logged-out redirect, the 301 slug redirect that must happen before any state change, the notification_level transitions (tracking or watching to regular, regular to muted), or a missing TopicUser row. The message_builder_spec change only passes an extra argument and does not assert that the link appears in the body or HTML. A spec that re-reads the topic_user row after unsubscribe would have caught the auto-track persistence bug.
